title: Relative adjoint character weights through all dual-number points
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $T,G$ be group schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, using the group-object diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. Let $i:T\to G$ be a homomorphism and $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_{m,A}$ a character, where $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ is [def-sfb-split-torus-over-ring]. For a commutative $A$-algebra $B$, use dual numbers [def-sc-dual-numbers]. Say that $\chi$ occurs in the adjoint tangent module over $B$ when there exists $v\in G(B[\epsilon])$ reducing to $1$ and different from $1$, such that for every $B$-algebra $C$ and $s\in T(C)$, $i(s)v_C i(s)^{-1}=\chi(s)\cdot v_C$. Here $v_C$ is obtained by the canonical map $B[\epsilon]\to C[\epsilon]$, and scalar multiplication by $c\in C$ is substitution $\epsilon\mapsto c\epsilon$. The scalar $\chi(s)$ is the value of the Laurent coordinate of the actual character. Equivalently this is the character eigenvector equation for the full adjoint coaction, not only the action on $A$-points. Define the nonzero adjoint weight set over $B$ to consist of the nontrivial characters that occur in this sense.
